title: Gates integration and hardening: the three human gates compose on one goal, and the shared roster is whole
description:
THE EPIC-FINAL ROW for epic-af14d735 (Operator gates and screens). Filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-05, at the human's direction, when this epic was split out of epic-8ebe6417 and left with no integration-and-hardening row of its own. Highest order in the epic; `get_context.isEpicFinal` should be true when you hold it.

WHY IT EXISTS. Verification on this board is CONCENTRATED, not smeared: mid-epic rows prove their own slice with focused tests and move on, and ONE row at the end gates the whole. The four band parents named in dependsOn (f3edb8fb Gate 2, 2a345b2e Gate 3, e7a20a49 control room, 8a6d6660 design) are each integration-shaped for their OWN band. Nothing in this epic currently tests what the bands got wrong ABOUT EACH OTHER, and that is exactly where this epic's risk lives, because all four bands write to the same shared roster files.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS - the four things no single slice could see:

1. THE SHARED ROSTER IS WHOLE. `preview.decide`, `release.decide`, `design.submit` and `design.read` each landed through packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, its hand-transcribed runtime-contract.test.ts, the regenerated control-room client, and the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors. Four rows moved the SAME count literals in sequence. Assert the end state is coherent: the runtime roster, the daemon PAYLOAD_KEYS served set, the registry, and the generated client agree in BOTH directions (global rail 9), and every digest mirror carries the CURRENT hex. The bidirectional set-equality is the point - a subset check passes while a served capability has silently vanished from the advertised surface.

2. THE THREE HUMAN GATES COMPOSE ON ONE GOAL. Gate 1 (product contract), the design step, Gate 2 (working preview) and Gate 3 (release) are four decisions in one operator's sequence. Prove the sequence end to end on a single goal against a real store: approve the contract, submit or SKIP a design, approve the preview, approve the release. That flow does not exist to be tested until every band has landed - which is what makes it this row's and not any slice's.

3. THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE HOLDS ACROSS ALL FOUR KINDS AT ONCE. Every gate kind must be operator-principal-only, MCP-excluded, and in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. Each band asserted its own; assert the SET. Enumerate the served kinds from the dispatch seam and assert that every gate kind is fenced on all three axes - a kind added to two of the three rosters is exactly the defect class that minted 8 junk goals live.

4. THE DOCS SWEEP for this epic, held back from the individual rows so the same file is not re-edited five times.

MEASURED CONTEXT AT FILING (2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa, branch moe/work-2026-09-04): 28 non-archived rows in this epic, 5 DONE, 20 WORKING, 3 BLOCKED. `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` is ONE Set at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195, re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts:24 - several task descriptions on this board still claim it is duplicated byte-for-byte, and that claim is STALE; re-measure before planning against it. The four digest mirrors at filing time were generated-client.ts:905, generated-coverage.test.ts:36, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18 and apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255 - THAT SET MOVES, so census it yourself with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types.

NOT IN SCOPE: building any gate. Every capability here is shipped by a row named in dependsOn. If this row finds a gap, the output is a prerequisite row measured symbol by symbol - never a narrowed DoD, never a mock-backed journey, and never authority reimplemented inside a test.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Run every leg named in DoD-6 and quote all their count lines.
definitionOfDone: FULL REGRESSION, green, with numbers, across every package this epic touched - `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and root `pnpm test`. Quote every `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING and is not evidence. State plainly that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file (vitest.config.ts:32 has no apps/** in its include), so the two app legs are not optional.

THE SHARED ROSTER IS COHERENT AT THE DELIVERED TREE, asserted in BOTH directions (global rail 9): enumerate the SERVED command kinds from the dispatch seam - not from the roster constant - and assert set-equality against the advertised runtime roster and the generated client. Deleting any one gate kind from either side must turn it red; prove that with a mutation drill rather than asserting it. Separately, census the GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types (a *.ts-only grep misses the .tsx mirror) and confirm every hit carries the CURRENT hex.

THE THREE HUMAN GATES COMPOSE ON ONE GOAL, proven end to end against a real store built by the production journey: Gate 1 approved, a design submitted OR skipped, the preview approved, the release approved. Assert the goal reaches the end state through the real command path - a journey that mocks any gate's authority proves the shape and retires the question unanswered. Assert the SKIPPED-design variant too: the loop must reach a release without a design.

THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE HOLDS FOR THE WHOLE SET AT ONCE. For every gate kind this epic published, assert all three axes together: operator-principal-only, MCP-excluded, and present in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. Enumerate the kinds from the implementation seam so a kind added to two of three rosters cannot pass. Assert an agent-authenticated dispatch is refused with its SPECIFIC reason code AND the layer that refused, never merely that it failed.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS over the WHOLE EPIC DIFF, looking for what the slices got wrong about each other rather than re-reviewing any one of them: a contract that drifted between producer and consumer; a refusal code whose layer disagrees across two bands; duplicated helpers that should have been shared; a count literal that two rows both moved; a gate whose offer is served but whose command path refuses it. Record what was checked and what was found - a pass that finds nothing must say what it looked for.

THE DOCS SWEEP for this epic, in ONE pass: the operator-facing words for all four gates, README/runbook if either now understates what the browser can do, and any doc that still describes a gate as unbuilt. Quote the files changed. If nothing needed changing, say which files were read to reach that conclusion.
taskRails: THIS ROW BUILDS NO GATE. Every capability it certifies is shipped by a row named in dependsOn. A gap found here becomes a prerequisite production row with the gap measured symbol by symbol - never a narrowed DoD, a mock-backed journey, or authority reimplemented inside a test. A proof that only proves shapes retires the question unanswered, and a falsely retired gate cannot be repaired.

ROSTER COVERAGE IS BIDIRECTIONAL OR IT IS NOTHING. Enumerate the served set from the dispatch seam, never from the roster constant: a test that iterates the roster shrinks its own iteration when an entry is deleted and stays green while a served capability vanishes from the advertised surface.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Every claim in this description about what exists on disk is STALE BY DEFAULT - including the digest-mirror list and the HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS note. Read the dependsOn rows' completionSummary and reviewSummary from get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring HEAD, and grep for anything they do not cover.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description:
GAP CENSUS FIRST — this row builds no gate, so its first act is to establish that every capability it certifies actually landed. All four dependsOn rows were WORKING at plan time; `dependsOn` gates the WORKING claim, but measure anyway.

For EACH gate kind this epic published — enumerate them from the epic's rows rather than from this plan, then measure each on all four surfaces:
  `git grep -n "<kind>" -- packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`
At plan time only `preview.decide` was present anywhere (shared contract only); `release.decide`, `design.submit` and `design.read` were absent from all three rosters. Expect that to have changed.

A kind present in the shared contract but not yet served by the daemon is a DOCUMENTED intermediate state, not a defect — `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-create-with-source.ts:35` records an existing kind in exactly that position. Do not file it.

IF A GATE IS GENUINELY MISSING at execution: STOP. The output is a PREREQUISITE PRODUCTION ROW with the gap measured symbol by symbol, filed in PLANNING with this row's id in its description, plus `moe.report_blocked` with `blockedOnTaskIds` naming it. Do NOT narrow the DoD, do NOT mock the gate's authority, and do NOT reimplement authority inside a test. A proof that only proves shapes retires the question unanswered, and a falsely retired gate cannot be repaired.

Also read each dependsOn row's `completionSummary` and `reviewSummary` through `get_context.epicSiblings` — the rails direct that read INSTEAD of re-measuring HEAD — and grep only for what they do not cover. Record the roster of kinds you found; every later step enumerates from it.

FULL REGRESSION BASELINE (DoD 1). Run every leg standalone and quote its `Test Files N passed` count line. An exit-0 leg with NO count line RAN NOTHING and is not evidence: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 when the package name is wrong, and "No test files found" is also exit 0.

- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`
- `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test` (root lane)

State plainly in the note that root `pnpm test` covers NO `apps/**` file — the root vitest include lists only `adapters/** packages/** tests/** tools/**` — so the two app legs are not optional and a bare root count line is never evidence for an apps/** claim.

Run this BEFORE writing any new arm, and keep the output: it is the merge-base half of the path-attributed baseline the completion record needs. Any red here that your diff did not cause is disclosed verbatim with its failing file paths, never hidden and never fabricated green.

DO NOT record these numbers as expectations anywhere in the code you write. Epic rail 3: four sibling rows move the same count literals in sequence and this row is last — a frozen count is one a concurrent row moves first.

THE SHARED ROSTER IS COHERENT, BOTH DIRECTIONS (DoD 2, first half). Write `apps/daemon/src/gates-roster-coherence.test.ts`.

Enumerate the SERVED set from the IMPLEMENTATION SEAM, never from a roster constant: the composed registry's keys (daemon-command-registry.ts:194 spreads the family handler tables) and `wiredMcpToolKinds()` (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:81, itself derived from `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` minus the exclusion). Assert SET EQUALITY against the advertised runtime roster and the generated client. A subset check passes while a served capability has silently vanished from the advertised surface; a test that iterates the roster shrinks its own iteration when an entry is deleted and stays green.

READ `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238` FIRST — it already asserts `[...v2.registry.keys()].sort()` equals `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` minus `planning.submit_decomposition`. If it already covers a direction, extend it or cite it rather than landing a duplicate arm with a second exclusion list that can drift.

DERIVE, DO NOT FREEZE. No count literal, no transcribed kind list in this file. Assert relationships between production surfaces so a sibling row bumping a roster cannot red this arm spuriously.

MUTATION DRILL, both directions, recorded in the step note: delete one gate kind from the ADVERTISED side and confirm RED; restore and prove it. Delete the same kind from the SERVED side (its handler-table entry) and confirm RED; restore and prove it. These are TRACKED files so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof; the new test file is UNTRACKED, so if you mutate it, back it up out of tree and prove the restore by SHA256 in a separate call.

THE DIGEST MIRROR CENSUS (DoD 2, second half) — as a COMMITTED ARM, not a transcript. A claim about files this row does not own is a premise unless it is a command that survives the commit and runs at the delivered tree.

Add an arm to `gates-roster-coherence.test.ts` that reads the digest from `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`, then reads each mirror file and asserts it carries THAT value — so the arm reds when a future regeneration leaves a mirror behind, instead of certifying a one-time grep.

CENSUS BY THE HEX, NEVER BY THE SYMBOL. Three of the four mirrors do not mention `GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` at all; they hard-code the value, and one is a `.tsx` that a `*.ts`-only grep cannot see. Run:
  D=$(grep -o '"[0-9a-f]\{64\}"' packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts | head -1 | tr -d '"')
  git grep -n "$D" -- . ':!.moe' ':!.serena'
At plan time this returned FOUR hits: generated-client.ts:907, packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts:36, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18, apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255. RE-RUN IT — that set moves, and the arm must enumerate the mirrors it finds rather than hard-coding this list.

Distinguish the two populations in the note: the three TRANSCRIBED mirrors above do NOT follow a regeneration and are hand edits; the symbol IMPORTERS (contract-pins.ts:7, contract-digest.test.ts:21, apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-{collector.ts,producers.test.ts}) DO follow automatically.

Two of the four live under apps/control-room, which is in none of `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` or the daemon leg — so `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is the only leg that can catch a stale one. Quote it here as well as in step 9.

THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE HOLDS FOR THE WHOLE SET AT ONCE (DoD 4). Write `apps/daemon/src/gates-human-only-fence.test.ts`.

Enumerate the gate kinds from the IMPLEMENTATION SEAM (the served registry keys filtered to this epic's kinds), not from a hand list, so a kind added to two of the three rosters cannot pass by being absent from the list the test iterates. For EVERY gate kind, assert ALL THREE AXES TOGETHER:
1. OPERATOR-PRINCIPAL-ONLY — present in `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:355).
2. MCP-EXCLUDED — absent from `wiredMcpToolKinds()`. Assert against that function, which computes the actual served-over-MCP surface (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:81), not against the exclusion roster: the exclusion list is DERIVED from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (:78), so asserting it against axis 1 would be circular and would pass with the fence broken.
3. HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS — present in the set at agent-spawn-contract.ts:195. Note this is ONE Set re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts, NOT a byte-for-byte duplicate; several task descriptions on this board still claim otherwise and that claim is stale.

A kind fenced on two of three axes is the defect class this arm exists for — it is what minted 8 junk goals live — so assert the three together per kind and report which axis failed, not merely that one did.

Then the REFUSAL: dispatch each gate kind with an AGENT-authenticated principal and assert the specific stable reason CODE and the LAYER that refused. Never merely that it failed — a test asserting only "refused" is one added layer away from vacuous, because a second refusal layer can answer first and the arm stays green while no longer testing its subject. Mutate the fence and confirm the arm reds.

THE THREE HUMAN GATES COMPOSE ON ONE GOAL (DoD 3, main variant). Write `apps/daemon/src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts`.

Against a REAL store built by the production journey, drive ONE goal through the operator's four decisions IN SEQUENCE, each through the REAL command path:
1. Gate 1 — `product_contract.approve_gate_1` (apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-command.ts).
2. The design step — `design.submit`.
3. Gate 2 — the working preview, `preview.decide`.
4. Gate 3 — the release, `release.decide`.
Assert the goal reaches the end state, and assert the ORDERING is enforced: attempting a later gate before its predecessor must refuse with its specific code and layer. A sequence that happens to pass when run in order proves less than one that refuses when run out of order.

MOCK NOTHING THAT DECIDES. A journey that mocks any gate's authority proves the shape and retires the question unanswered — that is the failure this row exists to prevent, and it is a rejection, not a shortcut. Test doubles are permitted only for things outside the decision path (a clock, a process launcher, a network call); every authority check runs its production code. State in the note exactly what was doubled and why each is not a decider.

Read the existing harnesses in tests/e2e/foundation/ (e2e-harness.ts, j1-loop-harness.ts, j3-crash-harness.ts, j4-replan-harness.ts) before inventing a fourth harness shape — reuse the store-construction pattern rather than a new one. Note they run in `pnpm test:e2e`, a different lane from this row's verification command.

Teardown: every store handle and temp directory released in a `finally`, on the throwing path too.

THE SKIPPED-DESIGN VARIANT (DoD 3, second half) — same file, its own arm. The loop must reach a release WITHOUT a design.

Drive a second goal: Gate 1 approved, the design SKIPPED, the preview approved, the release approved. Assert the goal reaches the same end state and that the skip is recorded on the aggregate rather than inferred from an absence — `task-365e5d978ba24c92a91b3ee19ab90558` (DONE, sha 70f9b643) shipped the skip as a recorded state whose decoder refuses a half-skipped revision, so assert against that recorded state and, if the decoder is reachable from here, assert a half-skipped revision is still refused with its code and layer.

ASSERT THE VARIANT ACTUALLY RAN. A swept or parameterised case that silently yields zero cases passes: if the two variants share a table, assert the table's length and that both branch labels executed. A skip that is implemented as "the arm did not run" is indistinguishable from a broken arm.

Then the negative: assert the SKIPPED path and the SUBMITTED path reach end states that differ where they should — the design version the plan was built on is present in one and explicitly absent in the other. Two paths that produce byte-identical end states would mean the design step changed nothing, which is a finding, not a pass.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE WHOLE EPIC DIFF (DoD 5). Not a re-review of any one row — look for what the four bands got wrong ABOUT EACH OTHER. All four wrote to the same shared roster files in sequence, and that is where this epic's risk lives.

Get the diff: `git log --oneline` for the epic's rows and a combined diff across every path they touched. Then hunt specifically for:
- A CONTRACT THAT DRIFTED between producer and consumer — a payload key the daemon reads that the client never sends, or a field the client sends that no handler reads.
- A REFUSAL CODE WHOSE LAYER DISAGREES across two bands — the same code attributed to different layers by two rows. Grep each gate's codes and compare their layer literals.
- A COUNT LITERAL TWO ROWS BOTH MOVED — check the hand-transcribed rosters (runtime-contract.test.ts, daemon-command-registry.test.ts, daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts) for a number that is right by luck: does the transcription's ORDER match the production tuple's sort? runtime-contract.test.ts:117-125 asserts sortedness against the production tuple precisely because a misplaced kind was once copied into the transcription and both stayed green.
- DUPLICATED HELPERS that should have been shared — four bands solving the same decode or fence problem four ways.
- A GATE WHOSE OFFER IS SERVED BUT WHOSE COMMAND PATH REFUSES IT — the affordance surface offering a step the dispatcher will not accept. Check each gate's offer against its handler.

RECORD WHAT WAS CHECKED AND WHAT WAS FOUND. A pass that finds nothing MUST say what it looked for — an unqualified "no issues found" is not a result. Put the list in a row comment (comments truncate silently at 5000 chars; keep it under ~4500). Anything found that is not this row's to fix becomes a prerequisite row or a comment, per DELIVERY BIAS — not a silent fix inside an epic-final row.

DOCS SWEEP (DoD 6) AND THE FINAL GATES — one pass, held back from the individual rows so the same file is not re-edited five times.

DOCS. Read `docs/VISION.md`, `docs/agent-stack-runbook.md` and `README.md` (the epic's plausible surface; also glance at docs/release-provenance.md if Gate 3 changed what a release carries). Update: the operator-facing WORDS for all four gates so the browser's vocabulary matches what shipped; the runbook and README if either now understates what the browser can do; and ANY doc that still describes a gate as unbuilt. Quote the files changed. IF NOTHING NEEDED CHANGING, name the files you READ to reach that conclusion — an unevidenced "docs are fine" is not a sweep.

FINAL GATES — re-run every leg from step 2 and quote every `Test Files N passed` count line:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.
The verification command recorded on `moe.complete_task` is `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Repeat that root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so the two app legs carry the apps/** claim.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: step 2's run is the merge-base half; this run is the HEAD half. Subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths, and complete only when that intersection is EMPTY. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths — as the epic-final row you will likely see peer red, and attributing it to this row is as wrong as hiding it.
